senses.sense_definition: A mathematical notation indicating the number of times a quantity is multiplied by itself.

examples.text: In the expression three to the fourth power, the number four is the <w>exponent</w>.
The teacher showed the students how to calculate expressions with a negative <w>exponent</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A person who supports, advocates, or represents a particular idea, theory, or belief.

examples.text: She was regarded as a leading <w>exponent</w> of modern architectural design.
The philosopher was an influential <w>exponent</w> of free-market economic policies.

senses.sense_definition: The component of a floating-point number representing the power of the base by which the mantissa is multiplied.

examples.text: In computer systems, eight bits are reserved to store the biased <w>exponent</w>.
An overflow occurs when the calculated <w>exponent</w> exceeds the maximum allowable value.

senses.sense_definition: The index specifying the degree of a root in a radical expression.

examples.text: The radical sign had an <w>exponent</w> of three to indicate a cube root.
When simplifying radical forms, determine the <w>exponent</w> of the root carefully.

senses.sense_definition: The linguistic realization or morphological manifestation of a grammatical feature.

examples.text: The suffix acts as an overt <w>exponent</w> of past tense in the verb paradigm.
The linguist analyzed which <w>exponent</w> marked the plural in this dialect.
